why: It is the most regulated shop in the catalogue and the one where a wrong number is a patient safety problem, so the pack has to earn trust before it earns money.
operator: The pharmacist of record runs the counter, checks prescriptions, and answers the same questions about the same medicine every day. Their day is pressure from two sides: a queue of people who need the medicine now, and a stock that expires in the back room because nobody could read the batch dates. The one thing that can end a career is a mistake, so they need the expiry and the interaction data to be right and to come from a real source.
entities: Pharmacy (id, name, branchId, address, phone, currency, licenseNumber, pharmacistOfRecord, taxRegistration)
Product (id, sku, barcode, nameAr, nameEn, genericName, activeIngredient, form, strength, unit, pricePiasters, taxRate, supplierId, reorderPoint, isControlled, isPrescriptionOnly)
Batch (id, productId, supplierId, quantity, receivedAt, expiryAt, costPiasters, purchaseOrderId)
Prescription (id, patientId, doctorName, clinicName, issuedAt, imageUrl, items, notes)
Patient (id, name, phone, nationalIdLast4, birthYear, chronicConditions, allergies, whatsappOptIn, consentGivenAt)
Sale (id, branchId, cashierId, patientId, lines, totalsPiasters, payments, createdAt, idempotencyKey)
SaleLine (id, saleId, productId, batchId, quantity, unitPricePiasters, isSubstitution)
Substitution (id, requestedProductId, offeredProductId, reason, acceptedBy, acceptedAt)
InteractionAlert (id, patientId, productIds, severity, source, acknowledgedBy, acknowledgedAt, actionTaken)
ControlledEntry (id, productId, batchId, quantity, reason, patientId, doctorName, loggedBy, createdAt, witnessName)
Supplier (id, nameAr, phone, paymentTerms, licenseNumber, lastOrderAt)
PurchaseOrder (id, supplierId, status, lines, expectedAt, totalPiasters)
Shift (id, branchId, openedBy, openedAt, closedAt, floatPiasters, countedPiasters)
Employee (id, name, phone, role, licenseNumber, status)
units: tablet, capsule, bottle, tube, box, strip, vial, sachet, millilitre, gram and the pack multiples the wholesalers use
batches: Every medicine is a batch with a received date, an expiry date and a purchase cost, because the expiry is the life of the shop and the cost per batch is what makes the margin true
expiry: The radar is the main screen of the sector: 7 days critical, 30 days watch, 90 days plan, with the batch, the quantity, the cost and the action (return to the supplier, discount, or keep). No medicine is sold from an expired batch
special: The structures specific to this sector are the patient profile with the chronic conditions and the allergies, the prescription with the doctor and the image, the drug interaction alert that a pharmacist acknowledges, the controlled drug log that is append only, and the substitution offer when a medicine is missing
screens: Pharmacy till: scan the barcode, see the batch that will be used, the patient name if the customer is a regular, and the price with the tax
Expiry radar: the batches that expire first with the quantity, the cost and one tap to return them to the supplier or to discount them
Prescription intake: photograph or scan the prescription, read the doctor, the date and the items, and turn it into a sale in one flow
Interaction check: when a medicine is added for a patient with a chronic condition, the alert appears with the source and the pharmacist decides
Controlled log: an append only list that never deletes a row, with the reason, the patient, the doctor and a second name as witness
Patient profile: the name, the phone, the conditions and the allergies, encrypted, with the purchase history and the export and delete buttons
Substitution: when a medicine is out of stock, the in stock generics with the same active ingredient and the same strength, and the price difference
Stock and suppliers: the items to reorder, the last purchase price and the supplier, and the returns to make
Shift close: the money, the controlled entries of the day and the sales count
roles: Owner (pharmacist of record): everything, including the staff, the prices and the reports, and the only role that can change the controlled log settings
Pharmacist: checks the prescription, acknowledges the interaction alerts, sells, and is the only role allowed to approve a substitution
Assistant (technician): sells an over the counter medicine, counts the stock, receives deliveries, cannot dispense a prescription only medicine
Cashier: takes the payment, closes the shift, no medicine advice
reports: Expiry loss in money, per batch and per supplier, with what was returned
Controlled entries for the day and the month, with the counts by substance
Top medicines by quantity and by margin, with the margin after the real batch cost
Prescription intake: how many, from which doctors, and the days of the month they arrive
Substitution rate: how often a missing medicine became a generic
Stock value at cost and at retail, and the reorder list
Shift summary with the cash variance and the sales count
integrations: Thermal printer through ESC/POS for the receipt and for the prescription label
Barcode scanner in keyboard mode, the standard for the medicine boxes

A real drug data source for the interaction rules: licensed and paid, or the feature stays off with an honest label (the legacy pharmacy shipped eight hand typed rules with no source, and that is banned)
WhatsApp for the prescription photo and the order confirmation through the pharmacy own account
ETA e receipt behind the server side signer, off until the specification is read
A secure store for the patient data with a per tenant key, never in the browser cache
onboarding: Business basics: name, branch, address, phone, currency
Licence: the pharmacy licence number and the pharmacist of record with the licence expiry
Catalog: import the medicines from a spreadsheet with the barcode, the generic name and the supplier
Batches: the first batches with their expiry dates, so the radar has something to show
Team: the pharmacist and the assistant with their permissions, and the pharmacist licence numbers
Suppliers: the main suppliers with their payment terms
First week plan: sell one item, receive one delivery with batches, print a receipt, acknowledge one alert in the test, set the reorder point
seed: Form and strength lists in Arabic (tablet, capsule, syrup, cream, injection) with the unit set for each
Role templates where the pharmacist alone can dispense and acknowledge
An empty patient list and an empty prescription list, never seeded with fake names
A receipt layout with the pharmacy header, the tax line and the medicine line with the strength
A controlled substance list left empty and marked as the pharmacist own list, because the real list is a legal document

landing_ar.headline: صيدلية تشوف التالف قبل ما يبقى خسارة، ومعلومات الأدوية من مصدر مرخّص

سجل الأدوية المراقَبة يُضاف إليه فقط: كل سطر فيه السبب والشاهد

landing_en.headline: A pharmacy that sees the expiry before it becomes a loss, and drug data from a licensed source
landing_en.sub: It runs on batches with their dates, and the controlled log can only be added to, never edited
benefits: The expiry screen shows the batches that go first with the quantity and the cost
The controlled log is append only: every row has the reason, the patient and a witness
An in stock generic with the same active ingredient and strength, with the price difference
faq: Where does the drug interaction data come from? From a licensed source, and when the source is not available the screen says so plainly instead of inventing an answer
Where is the patient data stored? Encrypted with a key per pharmacy, and it never enters a report or an AI question

pricing: The free tier covers the counter of a small pharmacy: one business, one branch, two seats, the till and the batch list
Starter adds a year of history and the expiry radar as a standing screen
The Business tier adds the patient profiles, the prescriptions, the substitution and the controlled log, because those are the parts that need more seats and more care
The licensed drug data source is priced separately and never bundled as if it were free

tasks.title: Register the pharmacy pack in the sector registry
tasks.brief: Add the manifest for pharmacy in packages/core/src/sectors/registry.ts with the base template pharmacy, the modules (pos, batches, fefo, patients, prescriptions, controlled log, alerts, suppliers), the feature flags, the role templates and the terminology map.
tasks.done: getSector('pharmacy') returns the manifest and the registry test asserts the modules and the pharmacist role.

tasks.title: Write the pharmacy data model with batches, patients and prescriptions
tasks.brief: Type the entities in packages/core/src/sectors/pharmacy/schema.ts: products with the active ingredient and the controlled flag, batches with the expiry and the cost, patients with the conditions and the allergies, prescriptions, interaction alerts and the controlled entry. Health fields are marked as encrypted and never enter analytics.
tasks.done: The schema compiles with no any, the encrypted fields are marked in the type, and the validation rejects a sale of an expired batch.

tasks.title: Build the pharmacy seed with the forms and the units
tasks.brief: Write packages/core/src/sectors/pharmacy/seed.ts with the Arabic forms and strengths, the unit set per form, the role templates where only the pharmacist dispenses, and the receipt layout. The patient list, the prescription list and the controlled substance list stay empty and marked as the pharmacist own documents.
tasks.done: The seed loads, the test asserts the forms and units, and it asserts that no patient, prescription or substance was invented.

tasks.title: Write the pharmacy terminology map in Arabic and English
tasks.brief: Create packages/ui/src/sector/pharmacy/glossary.ts with the pharmacy words: صيدلي, روشتة, جرعة, تركيز, صنف, منتهي الصلاحية, بديل, and the counter words, in Arabic and English.
tasks.done: The glossary covers every screen of the sector with no generic retail wording and the label test passes.

tasks.title: Build the expiry radar with the batch actions
tasks.brief: Build the expiry screen: the 7, 30 and 90 day bands, the batch with the quantity, the cost and the supplier, and the actions to return to the supplier or to discount, each written to the audit log with the user and the time.
tasks.done: The batches appear in the right order, the return records the batch as returned, the discount writes the audit entry, and an expired batch cannot be sold.

tasks.title: Build the prescription intake flow
tasks.brief: Build the intake: attach the prescription image, read the doctor, the clinic and the date, turn the items into the cart lines with the strength, and print the label. The image is stored in the secure store, not in the browser cache.
tasks.done: A prescription with two items creates a sale with two lines, the label prints with the doctor and the date, and the image is served through a signed URL that expires.

tasks.title: Build the patient profile with encryption and the export and delete
tasks.brief: Build the encrypted patient profile: the name, the phone, the chronic conditions and the allergies stored with the per tenant key, with the purchase history, and the export and delete actions that remove the record on request.
tasks.done: The conditions and the allergies are encrypted at rest, the values never appear in a report or in an AI prompt, and the delete removes the record and the audit trail keeps the fact of the delete without the content.

tasks.title: Build the interaction alert flow with a real source
tasks.brief: Build the alert flow: when the medicines for a patient are known, the alert service is asked, and the result is shown with its source and its severity, and the pharmacist acknowledges it with the action taken. With no licensed source configured, the screen says that clearly and produces no alert.
tasks.done: With a source configured the alert appears with the source and the acknowledgement is stored, and with no source the screen shows the honest state and invents nothing.

tasks.title: Build the append only controlled log
tasks.brief: Build the controlled substance log: an append only collection where no role can edit or delete a row, with the substance, the batch, the quantity, the reason, the patient, the doctor, the witness and the timestamp, plus the daily count report.
tasks.done: An edit or a delete attempt is refused by the rules and by the code, the count report matches the rows, and the audit log records every attempt.

tasks.title: Build the pharmacy report pack and the substitution screen
tasks.brief: Add the reports of this sector: expiry loss by batch and supplier, the controlled entries by substance and day, the top medicines by quantity and by real margin, the prescriptions by doctor and the substitution rate, each with the CSV export, and build the substitution screen that offers the in stock generics with the same ingredient and strength.
tasks.done: The reports compute their own numbers, the test matches a manual calculation, and the substitution list only shows products that are really in stock.

risks: The drug interaction and substitution data must come from a licensed source or be clearly marked as unverified: inventing a clinical answer is a patient safety risk and it is banned
Patient data is special category: encrypted per tenant, never in analytics, never in an AI prompt, exported and deleted on request
The controlled log is append only, and the pharmacist of record is the only role that can change its settings
The pharmacy licence and the pharmacist licence numbers are stored as the shop wrote them and are never checked by us with any claim of validation
